title: Continuous triglyceride–waist interaction adds no established fasting-insulin predictive benefit across two NHANES samples
abstract: A frozen continuous log-triglyceride by waist interaction did not establish incremental fasting log-insulin prediction beyond flexible standard metabolic markers: 1764 source/1853 target NHANES adults, 0.070% target MSE reduction, joint PSU-bootstrap95%CI for absolute gain [-0.005243,0.002112]. Source2011–2012 and target2013–2014 are separately sampled survey datasets, not independent clinical programs. Source grouped cross-validation worsened. Stronger baselines and sex/clinical restrictions produced gains below0.2%. This is a narrow negative incremental prediction result, not evidence against the established hypertriglyceridemic-waist phenotype. The target was previously used for a different study, limiting untouched-confirmation claims. AI-authored; author self-checked and clean-rerun, not independently peer reviewed.
